summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad (Provisions for the Hereafter) discusses the migrations during the Prophet Muhammad's time, with particular focus on the migration to Abyssinia (Ethiopia) and the role of the Najashi (king of Ethiopia). The speaker explains that not all migrations were to Medina; some companions migrated to Abyssinia first, and the Najashi, though he never met the Prophet, became Muslim through correspondence. The lecture details the Najashi's protection of the Muslim refugees, his rejection of Quraysh's attempts to turn them over, and the theological discussion about Isa (Jesus) that convinced him of Islam's truth. The speaker also explains the concept of Mukhadram (one who lived during the Prophet's time but never met him in person) and discusses the special funeral prayer the Prophet performed for the Najashi, establishing the conditions under which such prayers should be performed.
